column1: # rescue-stress dispositions: the wrong outputs the gate tolerates, and its pins.
# Compiled into `cargo run -p xtask -- rescue-stress`. Every published
# detection of a grid cell is one output; an output that is not the cell's
# truth needs a row here, or the run fails (open). A row holds only while its
# exact output occurs (pass, cell, label, kind, path, symbology, content_sha256,
# text_sha256, text_len and engines); a row whose output no longer occurs
# fails the run too (stale). Delete a row in the same change that clears its output. Every
# row carries a public reason. A release qualifies only with no rows left.
# Pins, one of each per pass (uncapped, capped, dual), before the column
# header: `floor` is the exact strict_correct (cells that publish exactly
# their ASCII truth bytes/text as qr_code, with a known non-lossy charset and no
# ECI/FNC1 declarations); `engine_panics` is the exact sum of
# report.trace.engine_panics; `caught_panics` is the exact count the process
# panic hook sees, which also covers the score-probe panics that
# report.trace.engine_panics drops. Every pin fails in either direction (a
# strict_correct above its floor too) and moves only together with its cause.
# Columns are tab-separated. kind: qr_wrong (a wrong QR, no truth output in
# the cell), qr_extra (a wrong QR beside the truth), rescue_qr (a wrong QR
# from the S5 rescue), non_qr (any other symbology). path: rescue when the
# engines include the rescue, else engine. Only the dual pass may hold a
# rescue-path row: the uncapped and capped passes fail on any rescue-path
# wrong output. content_sha256 identifies the complete published content
# using the versioned encoding in rescue_stress.rs: raw bytes, exact charset,
# ordered ECI declarations (including starts/duplicates and None versus []),
# FNC1 and text. text_sha256/text_len separately identify its UTF-8 text.
